Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training. (Required)
Knowledge of and experience with and/or the ability to learn Admissions software systems (e.g., Slate).
Experience with and/or the ability to creating/maintaining SIS reports and queries (like using PeopleSoft Query Manager).
Experience and comfort working with various staff and both technical and functional experts. Ability to collaborate effectively.
Understands the graduate student lifecycle; experience in higher education.

The Business Systems Analyst serves as a systems analyst for the Graduate Division's interconnected Student Services departments' business systems, supporting Admissions, Funding, Degrees, Appointments, and Student Life. This position combines student information systems expertise with knowledge of Graduate Division business processes and operational needs to support system functionality, process design, documentation, testing, requirements gathering, training, and continuous improvement. The Business Systems Analyst serves as a liaison between Graduate Division subject matter experts and the central campus Student Information Systems unit, represents the Graduate Division in relevant user groups, maintains documentation of critical system processes and behaviors, tracks and monitors ticket progress, and identifies opportunities to improve system functionality, data integrity, and operational efficiency.
Student Services Systems Support - 25%

This position applies seasoned professional knowledge of business processes, student information systems, and organizational policies and procedures to resolve a broad range of moderate to complex operational and systems issues. Uses sound judgment to analyze problems, identify appropriate solutions, and recommend improvements. Works closely with Student Services staff to address systems issues affecting admissions, degrees, student employment, funding, and student life. Serves as a knowledgeable resource across Student Services, translating policy and operational needs into effective systems and process solutions.

Works closely with Student Services advisors & IT Partners to troubleshoot complex systems and business-process issues. Systems and tools include Campus Solutions, Slate, eForms, Academic Progress Report (APR), queries, and student-record/data storage.

Knowledgeable about system functionality, configuration, tables, routing, integrations, data integrity, dependencies, specialized queries, and expected system behavior. Serves as a resource for complex systems questions and issues supporting admissions, funding, degrees, appointments, and academic progress.

Assists Student Services advisors with reporting escalation and follow up on issues (gaps, defects, dependencies, and opportunities for enhancement) to SIS for further investigation. Helps coordinate resolution, develop & document workarounds or escalate issues as appropriate.
Facilitates the development of queries and reporting tools to support Student Services operations and data integrity.

Works with other Graduate Division BSAs to understand the functionality of various systems used within Student Services and cross-trains with other technical staff to enable backup and support as necessary.
Catalogs and maintains a record of the Student Services systems-reliant processes. This includes queries/reports, batch processes, QBUs, and APIs.
Functional/Technical Translation - 25%
Gathers, analyzes, and documents business and user requirements and translates them into functional specifications.
Applies knowledge of graduate student policies, procedures, business processes, and system functionality to identify appropriate system solutions.
Communicates technical changes, limitations, dependencies, and system impacts to functional staff (or GSAOs when needed) in clear and actionable terms.
Partners with Student Services leadership and subject matter experts to identify, evaluate, prioritize, and plan system improvements and enhancements.
Represents Graduate Division (along with SMEs colleagues) and participates in applicable SIS User Groups or ad-hoc meetings.
Monitors, documents, and follows up on tickets escalated to them from student services staff.
Serves as a knowledgeable resource to less-experienced systems staff and functional users.
Business Process Improvement - 25%
Analyzes trends in system issues, user needs, data, and processing to identify opportunities for improvement.

Recommends and implements changes to business processes, procedures, and system functionality in partnership with subject matter experts and SIS. Confers with Assistant Dean for Student Services and unit directors on prioritization of efforts.
Leads or contributes to the development of improved workflows, specifications, documentation (job aids and/or user guides), and operational resources.
Develops sustainable solutions to recurring issues by addressing root causes rather than relying solely on temporary workarounds.
Evaluates and prioritizes potential enhancements based on business need, policy requirements, operational impact, feasibility, and benefit to Student Services.
Maintains awareness of emerging system and process needs and makes recommendations to Student Services leadership regarding future improvements.
Uses AI to create user knowledge bases and automate business processes
Plans, coordinates, and executes functional and user acceptance testing for system, eForm, APR, milestone, and related changes.
Develops and maintains testing scripts and scenarios informed by Student Services Advisors and related to system behavior, trends, business processes, and anticipated user activity.
Partners with subject matter experts and SIS to implement and monitor system changes and enhancements.
Supports staff through changes to systems, processes, and procedures to promote consistent implementation and minimize disruption to operations.
Professional Development and Participation - 5%
Participates in Graduate Division staff meetings, retreats and professional development.
Attends and seeks professional development opportunities like training and conferences.
Knowledge of and/or the ability to learn various modules within PeopleSoft Campus Solutions, including Records & Enrollment, Financial Aid, and Academic Advisement to support staff advisors.
Self-motivated worker with ability to work independently and as part of a team. Able to learn effectively and meet deadlines. Demonstrates problem-solving skills.

Demonstrates effective communication and social perceptiveness, awareness and comprehension of others reactions. Demonstrated ability to communicate technical information to technical and non-technical personnel at various levels in the organization verbally and in writing.
Demonstrated knowledge of and/or the ability to learn IT collaboration & ticketing systems (such as JIRA, Slack, and ServiceNow).
Demonstrated testing and test planning skills.
Demonstrated data analysis skills and tools.
Strong skills and knowledge of methodologies associated with analysis of processes and problems, information flow, and architecture.
Ability to identify, document, and develop original ideas to solve problems.
